newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Germany's Nord LB plans NLG 500 mln bond soon.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Nord LB plans NLG 500 mln bond soon.

text.p: Norddeutsche Landesbank said on Monday it planned its first ever bond denominated in guilders as soon as market conditions were right.
Nord LB management board member Juergen Koesters said the German bank was planning a 500 million guilder issue with a maturity of seven to 10 years.
Koesters said the bank was strengthening its funding in other European currencies as part of an investor relations campaign ahead of European economic and monetary union (EMU).

He told a news conference that the bank -- which has also issued its first French franc and Spanish peseta bonds during the last 18 months -- expected to face more competition from foreign borrowers in the German market once EMU went ahead.

The bank's senior vice-president for capital markets Hans-Joachim Habben said Nord LB expected to increase its foreign currency borrowings to 25-35 percent of total borrowings by the time EMU begins from 13-14 percent now.
